title: Paella Valenciana
subtitle: Traditional Spanish rice with chicken and rabbit
excerpt: The original paella: not the seafood version beloved by tourists, but the Valencian original of chicken, rabbit, green beans, and butter beans cooked with rice in a wide, flat pan over an open wood fire until the socarrat forms on the base.

recipe.sourceNotes: Paella is the signature dish of the Valencia region of Spain, and the traditional Valencian version (paella valenciana) contains chicken and rabbit with green beans and butter beans — not seafood. The dish originated among farmers and labourers in the rice paddies of the Albufera region south of Valencia, and takes its name from the wide, shallow two-handled iron pan (paellera) in which it is cooked. The defining feature of a correctly made paella is the socarrat — the layer of slightly caramelised, crispy rice that forms on the bottom of the pan at the end of cooking. Paella is cooked over high heat and the rice must not be stirred once the stock has been added; stirring releases the starch and prevents the socarrat forming.

content.text: Never stir the rice once the stock has been added. The paella should not be covered; the water must evaporate to develop the socarrat. If using a standard hob burner, rotate the pan a quarter-turn every few minutes to distribute the heat as evenly as possible. Short-grain Valencian rice (bomba or calasparra) is essential; long-grain rice gives a completely different result.

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan or large shallow frying pan over high heat. Brown the chicken pieces on all sides. Push to the edges. Add the green beans and cook for 2 minutes. Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until the tomato has reduced.
Add the paprika. Pour in the hot stock and saffron water. Add the butter beans. Season. Distribute the rice evenly across the pan. Do not stir. Bring to a rolling boil and cook for 5 minutes.

Reduce the heat to medium and cook for a further 15 minutes without stirring. The rice should have absorbed all the stock and be just cooked. Raise the heat for the final 2 minutes to develop the socarrat. Remove from the heat and rest for 5 minutes. Serve from the pan.
